hero.headline: SoftBank to invest up to $75 billion in French data centers
hero.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to $75 billion to build data centers in France. The investment will focus on developing and operating up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity.

The Japanese technology conglomerate made the commitment as demand for data infrastructure continues to grow globally. Data centers house the servers and computing equipment that power internet services, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence systems.

The planned 5 gigawatts of capacity would represent a significant expansion of data center infrastructure in France. Gigawatts measure electrical power consumption, with larger data centers requiring massive amounts of electricity to run servers and cooling systems.

SoftBank has been active in infrastructure investments globally, with holdings spanning telecommunications, technology ventures, and energy projects. The firm has previously invested billions in technology companies and infrastructure through its Vision Fund and other investment vehicles.

France has been working to attract major technology investments as European nations compete to build out digital infrastructure. Data centers have become critical infrastructure for supporting everything from streaming services to corporate computing needs.

The investment timeline and specific locations for the planned data centers were not disclosed in the announcement. SoftBank stated the investment represents an upper limit of up to $75 billion, though the firm did not provide details on how the spending would be phased or what conditions might affect the final total.

The scale of the investment would make it one of the largest data center buildouts announced in Europe. Technology companies and infrastructure investors have been racing to expand data center capacity to meet growing demand from cloud services and artificial intelligence applications, which require substantial computing power and data storage.

cards.headline: Tentative US-Iran deal would extend ceasefire, reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: The U.S. and Iran reached a preliminary agreement this week that could extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though final approval remains uncertain.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

The U.S. and Iran have moved closer to extending their current ceasefire, a development that has already affected global markets. News of the potential agreement prompted oil prices to fall on Thursday as investors reacted to the possibility of renewed stability in the region.

President Trump holds the key to whether this deal will move forward. The tentative agreement would extend the ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though unresolved core issues remain between the two nations. The emerging deal is expected to be a major focus of Sunday political discussions.

cards.headline: Trump sends revised terms to Iran as negotiations continue
cards.teaser: The president has delivered tougher conditions to Iran for a peace framework as the war enters its fourth month.
cards.body:
President Trump has sent revised terms to Iran as part of ongoing negotiations for a peace framework, according to officials. The new conditions represent a toughening of the American position as discussions continue.

The war between the United States and Iran has now entered its fourth month. Trump entered the Situation Room to make what officials described as a final determination on a potential Iran deal. The negotiations have produced mixed signals from the administration as the conflict continues.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during test, leaving NASA moon program reliant on SpaceX
cards.body:
A New Glenn rocket owned by Blue Origin exploded on a launchpad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday evening, damaging NASA's plans to establish a lunar base and return astronauts to the moon within the next two years.

The explosion occurred at 9 p.m. ET during a static fire test, when the rocket remains anchored to the ground. A massive fireball destroyed the launchpad at Kennedy Space Center, creating an orange sky visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away. Shockwaves from the blast were felt across Florida's space coast, with residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reporting that their homes shook. Emergency officials confirmed there was no threat from fumes or other hazards.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos said all company employees were accounted for and safe. He described the incident as "a very rough day" and said the company was investigating the cause, calling it an "anomaly."

The timing of the explosion creates significant complications for NASA. Just hours before the blast, Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of the $20 billion moon base. The New Glenn rocket is intended to launch landers to the lunar surface for NASA's Artemis program.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said a full evaluation of mission timelines would be conducted following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he wrote on social media.

The setback strengthens SpaceX's position in the competition for lunar contracts. SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System is already competing with Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander to determine which will transport the Artemis IV crew to the lunar surface in 2028. NASA had been working to diversify its launch options to avoid depending on any single company, but the explosion now leaves SpaceX as the only operational option for the agency's near-term moon exploration plans.

This is the latest in a series of problems for Blue Origin. Last month, a payload from the company's third New Glenn flight ended up in the wrong orbit, triggering a temporary grounding by the Federal Aviation Administration. Thursday's static fire test was the first since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight.

Elon Musk, SpaceX's founder and owner of the social media platform where much commentary appeared, simply wrote "Most unfortunate" and "Rockets are hard."

Blue Origin and SpaceX have both constructed large facilities near Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions in partnership with NASA.

cards.headline: New car sales drop for eighth consecutive month as one million buyers exit market
cards.teaser: The American auto market has lost one million buyers, with sales declining for eight straight months amid falling EV demand and financial pressure on consumers.
cards.body:
The United States auto industry has seen one million buyers disappear from the new car market, marking the eighth consecutive month of declining sales. Industry analysts indicate these customers are not expected to return soon, representing a structural shift in the automotive market.

Electric vehicle demand has collapsed as part of the broader downturn, while consumers face mounting financial pressure. The sustained sales decline suggests that purchasing a new car has become unaffordable for a growing segment of the American population, fundamentally changing the market dynamics for automakers.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Reaches 245 Suspected Deaths
cards.body:
More than 245 people are suspected to have died from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with 246 suspected cases reported in Ituri province. The outbreak has prompted international health organizations to mobilize emergency response teams to support local health workers in the region.

The World Health Organization director visited the worst-affected area as the medical charity Doctors Without Borders described the spread as deeply alarming. The WHO estimates the death rate at between 30 percent and 50 percent based on confirmed cases. Health workers in the area face significant challenges, lacking adequate protective equipment and treatment supplies to handle the outbreak effectively.

The virus has spread across multiple communities in eastern Congo, with cases reported mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones as well as the neighboring city of Bunia. The outbreak represents one of the deadliest Ebola events in recent years, with transmission continuing despite containment efforts.

Ituri province presents particular difficulties for disease control. The region is a mining hub where thousands of people work in close proximity, and ongoing armed conflict has displaced populations into overcrowded camps. This combination of factors creates conditions that make controlling transmission extremely challenging. The virus has already spread beyond the DRC, with Uganda confirming cases after a 59-year-old man died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the affected region.

A significant concern is the strain of Ebola involved in this outbreak. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed that samples tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain, for which no licensed vaccine exists. This differs from the more common Zaire strain found in previous DRC outbreaks. Only two previous outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus occurred, in 2007 and 2012.

International health organizations are working to establish treatment centers and trace contacts of infected individuals. Medical teams are focusing on isolating patients, implementing safe burial practices, and vaccinating at-risk populations to slow the virus's spread. The Africa CDC convened an urgent meeting with authorities from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, along with the WHO and pharmaceutical companies, to coordinate regional response efforts.

Ebola is a severe viral disease spread through direct contact with body fluids of infected people or dead bodies, particularly during funeral preparations. The virus has a high fatality rate, as demonstrated by the 2014-16 west African outbreak that resulted in approximately 28,000 cases and 11,000 deaths.

The WHO's visit and the convening of regional coordination meetings signal international recognition of the outbreak's severity. Officials have emphasized that rapid coordination across borders is essential given the population movement between affected areas and neighboring countries.

cards.headline: Israeli Soldiers Describe Ongoing Killings in Gaza Despite Ceasefire
cards.teaser: Soldiers shared rare firsthand accounts with reporters, calling the ceasefire agreement a joke.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided rare direct accounts to the Associated Press describing continued military operations in Gaza following an announced ceasefire. One soldier characterized the agreement as a joke, suggesting the fighting has not actually ceased.

The soldiers' willingness to speak publicly offers an uncommon perspective on conditions on the ground. Military personnel typically avoid discussing ongoing operations with journalists, making these interviews noteworthy for assessing how the ceasefire has been implemented in practice.

cards.teaser: A drone struck a residential building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war directly into civilian homes.
cards.body:
The Guardian article is about a completely different incident — a drone show failure at Vivid Sydney in Australia, not a Russian drone crashing into a Romanian apartment building.

I'm returning your original card text unchanged:

A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, causing a fire and panic among residents. The incident brought the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war into direct contact with Romanian civilians, reminding them of the dangers of living near an active conflict zone.

The crash produced a loud explosion and started a fire in the building. Romania shares a border with Ukraine, making it vulnerable to spillover from the war between Russia and Ukraine.

cards.headline: Colombian Presidential Election Sunday Tests Left's Regional Strength
cards.teaser: Voters head to polls with a leftist candidate leading but facing a surging far-right challenger.
cards.body:
Colombia holds its presidential election on Sunday as a significant moment for left-wing political movements across Latin America. The leftist candidate leads in polling, but faces a strong challenge from a far-right outsider who calls himself "The Tiger" and has gained recent momentum.

The election has drawn regional attention, with Ecuador's leader Daniel Noboa facing accusations of interfering in the vote. Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with the right-wing presidential candidate, raising questions about foreign involvement ahead of Sunday's polling.

cards.headline: French Intellectual Edgar Morin Dies at 104
cards.teaser: The former Resistance member became one of France's most influential thinkers across multiple disciplines.
cards.body:
Edgar Morin, a French intellectual known as the grandfather of French intellectuals, has died at 104. He was a former member of the Resistance during World War II and went on to a career that spanned multiple eras and academic disciplines.

Morin's books and public statements carried significant moral authority in France. His work crossed traditional academic boundaries, and he remained an active voice in French intellectual life for decades after the war.

cards.headline: Rescuers Free Four More Miners From Flooded Laos Cave
cards.teaser: The rescue mission continues for gold miners trapped underground for 10 days, with two still missing.
cards.body:
Rescue teams have freed four more miners from a flooded cave in Laos, bringing the total number of survivors to five out of seven men who entered the tunnels on May 20 seeking gold. The men spent 10 days trapped underground before divers reached them in difficult conditions.

Two miners remain missing as rescue efforts continue. Divers are navigating through narrow, water-filled tunnels filled with sharp rocks and collapse hazards to locate them. The operation has required teams to drain water from the cave system to access deeper sections.

cards.headline: Ecuador Accused of Election Interference Over Colombia Tariff Offer
cards.teaser: Ecuador's president offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing Colombian candidate ahead of Sunday's vote.
cards.body:
Ecuador has been accused of interfering in Colombia's presidential election after President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs following a conversation with a right-wing presidential candidate. The offer came just days before Sunday's vote.

The accusation raises questions about whether Ecuador's tariff pledge constitutes inappropriate meddling in a neighboring country's electoral process. Colombia's presidential election is taking place on Sunday, with the tariff issue potentially affecting voters in border regions.

hero.headline: Bus driver charged with manslaughter in Virginia crash that killed five
hero.body:
A bus driver has been charged with manslaughter following a crash on Interstate 95 in Virginia that killed five people and injured 44 others. The driver, identified as Jing S. Dong, was operating the bus when the collision occurred in Stafford County.

Among the dead were members of a family of four traveling to a wedding. The victims included Dmitri and Ecaterina Doncev, along with Priscilla Mafalda. The family was on their way to attend a wedding when the crash happened.

Investigators from the National Transportation Safety Board said a high rate of speed was a factor in the crash. Witnesses described the bus as traveling at an excessive speed before the collision. One witness told investigators the bus was going really fast.

The crash left 44 people injured in addition to the five fatalities. The collision took place on Interstate 95, a major highway corridor that runs along the East Coast. The NTSB investigation into the crash remains ongoing.

Authorities have not released additional details about the circumstances leading up to the collision or whether other factors contributed to the crash. The charges against Dong follow an initial assessment of the incident by law enforcement and safety investigators.

The crash represents one of the deadlier highway incidents in Virginia in recent memory. Interstate 95 in the Stafford County area is a heavily traveled route connecting Northern Virginia with areas farther south. The NTSB typically conducts thorough investigations of transportation accidents involving multiple casualties.

The wedding the family had been planning to attend was disrupted by the sudden loss. Details about the other victim who died in the crash have not been made public. The 44 injured passengers were transported to area hospitals, though the extent of their injuries has not been disclosed by authorities.

cards.teaser: The president has delivered tougher conditions to Iran for a peace framework as the war enters its fourth month.

cards.headline: Graham Platner's wife confirms he sent explicit texts to other women during marriage
cards.teaser: The Maine Senate candidate's wife has acknowledged her husband sent sexually explicit messages to other women as his campaign began.
cards.body:
Amy Gertner, wife of Maine's Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner, has confirmed that her husband exchanged sexually explicit texts with other women while they were married. She flagged the messages to his Senate campaign last year as his race was beginning.

Platner, an oyster farmer and former US Marine, is Maine's presumptive Democratic nominee for the Senate. Gertner has said publicly that she is deeply hurt by the revelations. The campaign has acknowledged that Platner sent the sexual texts while married.

cards.headline: Arsenal loses Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain in penalty shootout
cards.teaser: Gabriel's first penalty attempt for Arsenal ended in a miss that handed PSG their second consecutive Champions League title.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain retained their Champions League title by defeating Arsenal on penalties in the final. The match went to a shootout after regulation time, with both teams unable to break the deadlock.

Arsenal's Eberechi Eze and Gabriel both missed their penalty kicks, proving costly in the shootout. Gabriel's miss was particularly significant as it came in his first penalty for Arsenal. PSG's victory marked their second consecutive Champions League triumph, dashing Arsenal's hopes of winning the competition for the first time in their history.

cards.headline: Cuba's power outages trap elderly residents in high-rise buildings
cards.teaser: Rolling blackouts have left apartment dwellers unable to use elevators, creating hardship for older residents.
cards.body:
Power outages across Cuba have created a dangerous situation for residents living in high-rise apartment buildings, leaving them unable to use elevators during blackouts. A 70-year-old widow recounted how a power failure trapped her and her husband in their building when he needed medical attention, preventing them from accessing the care he required.

The recurring blackouts have become a persistent problem affecting daily life throughout the country, leaving residents facing ongoing uncertainty about when electricity will be restored.

cards.headline: Ferrari faces criticism over first electric vehicle design
cards.teaser: The Italian carmaker's Luce EV has drawn backlash from critics who say it departs from Ferrari's traditional identity.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, has faced significant criticism since its introduction. The car was designed to compete with Chinese electric vehicles in the growing EV market.

Critics have said the Luce represents a departure from Ferrari's roots. The backlash has focused on design choices that some say abandon the brand's traditional identity. Ferrari had positioned the vehicle as its entry into the electric car segment, but public reception has been negative.

cards.headline: Newly discovered fungus may help restore British habitats invaded by moss
cards.teaser: Scientists have identified a fungal species that could potentially reverse damage caused by invasive moss in native ecosystems.
cards.body:
A newly discovered species of fungus has raised hopes that some native British habitats could be restored after being decimated by invasive moss. The fungus appears to target the problematic moss that has overtaken certain ecosystems.

Researchers have described the organism as a potential solution to habitat degradation. The discovery offers a possible biological control method for areas where invasive moss has displaced native plant species. Scientists are studying whether the fungus can be used to help damaged habitats recover.

cards.teaser: The Japanese investment firm will invest up to 75 billion euros in French data centers, creating what would be Europe's biggest AI infrastructure facility.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build artificial intelligence data centers in France, positioning the country as a major hub for AI infrastructure in Europe. The investment represents one of the largest commitments to AI infrastructure on the continent.

The Japanese technology company aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity through the project. The massive facilities will support the computational demands of artificial intelligence applications.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempts to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight heading to Minneapolis was diverted to Wisconsin after a 75-year-old passenger made multiple attempts to enter the cockpit.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight heading to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin, after a passenger made multiple attempts to breach the cockpit. The 75-year-old man repeatedly tried to access the restricted area during the flight, prompting crew members to restrain him for safety reasons.

The plane landed in Madison where the passenger was detained. The FBI indicated that no criminal charges are expected at this time.

cards.headline: Sound Transit revises light rail expansion plan amid affordability concerns
cards.teaser: The transit agency passed a revised plan for Seattle-area light rail projects after determining the original expansion was no longer affordable.
cards.body:
Sound Transit's board approved changes to its ST3 light rail expansion program, shelving some projects including the Ballard line. The agency cited affordability concerns in outlining the future of its light rail construction plans, prompting questions from taxpayers about refunds for the scaled-back program.

Seattle City Council members have pledged to continue advocating for the Ballard Light Rail despite its removal from the immediate construction schedule. The revised plan aims to keep light rail expansion moving forward on a more financially sustainable timeline, though the scope will be reduced from original commitments.

cards.headline: China's clinical drug trials draw attention as biotech industry expands
cards.teaser: Clinical trials conducted in China are gaining prominence at an international oncology conference, raising concerns about waning US dominance in biotechnology.
cards.body:
Chinese pharmaceutical research received significant attention at an international oncology gathering in Chicago, where clinical trials from China were prominently featured. The country's biotechnology industry has grown rapidly, fueling concerns among American industry observers about the United States losing its leading position in drug development.

China's rise in pharmaceutical research and development represents a shift in the global biotech landscape. The increased presence of Chinese clinical trials at major international medical conferences signals the country's growing capabilities in developing new treatments and conducting large-scale medical research.

cards.headline: Ferrari faces criticism over first electric vehicle design
cards.teaser: The Italian automaker's Luce EV has drawn backlash from critics who say the design abandons Ferrari's traditional roots.
cards.body:
Ferrari unveiled its first electric vehicle, the Luce, as part of its strategy to compete with Chinese EV manufacturers. The vehicle has faced heavy criticism since its introduction, with detractors arguing that the design represents a departure from the brand's heritage.

The luxury carmaker had positioned the Luce as its answer to the growing electric vehicle market, particularly competition from Chinese manufacturers. The negative response highlights the challenges traditional automotive brands face when transitioning to electric powertrains while maintaining their established design identity.

cards.headline: GitHub switches Copilot to token-based billing
cards.teaser: Microsoft's GitHub changed its billing model for Copilot, drawing criticism from developers.
cards.body:
GitHub has shifted Copilot's pricing model from a flat subscription fee to token-based billing, where users pay according to the amount of text their AI assistant processes. The move has drawn significant backlash from developers, with many expressing frustration over the change.

The new billing structure makes Copilot's costs more transparent and variable, potentially increasing expenses for heavy users. Microsoft, which owns GitHub, continues to expand Copilot integration across its developer tools and services.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels investment fund
cards.teaser: Twenty alumni from Snap formed a new fund to invest in social media startups.
cards.body:
A group of 20 Snap alumni has launched Ghost Angels, a new investment fund focused on backing the next generation of social media companies. The fund combines capital with hands-on expertise from former team members who worked on Snapchat, one of the world's major social platforms.

The fund aims to support early-stage social media ventures with resources and knowledge drawn from the founders' experience at Snap.

cards.headline: Fungus species could help restore habitats damaged by invasive moss
cards.teaser: A newly discovered fungus species may enable restoration of British habitats affected by invasive moss.
cards.body:
Scientists identified a fungus species that could help restore native British habitats damaged by invasive moss. The discovery offers potential for reversing ecological damage in affected areas.

The fungus targets invasive moss that has decimated some native habitats in Britain. Researchers believe the species could provide a biological control method for managing the invasive moss and allowing native plants to recover.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases backward compatibility updates for Switch games on Switch 2
cards.teaser: Nintendo issued a new batch of fixes enabling Switch games to run better on Switch 2.
cards.body:
Nintendo released another wave of backward compatibility fixes for original Switch games running on the Switch 2 console. The updates address issues that affected how older titles perform on the newer hardware.

The Switch 2 is designed to play games from the original Switch library. Nintendo has been issuing periodic updates to improve how legacy games function on the new system.

cards.headline: YouTube directors helm two biggest movies of the weekend
cards.teaser: The top two films at the box office were both directed by people who started on YouTube.
cards.body:
The two highest-grossing movies of the weekend were directed by filmmakers who began their careers on YouTube. Both films fall into the horror genre.

The success represents a continued trend of YouTube creators transitioning into traditional film production. Several content creators who built audiences on the video platform have moved into directing feature films in recent years.

cards.headline: Infinity Ward says Modern Warfare 4 will avoid celebrity crossover content
cards.teaser: The game developer stated the next Call of Duty title will maintain a realistic aesthetic.
cards.body:
Infinity Ward announced that Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will not feature celebrity characters or crossover content from other franchises. The developer specifically ruled out skins based on Lady Gaga, Nicki Minaj, and the character Omni-Man.

The studio emphasized its commitment to keeping Modern Warfare 4 grounded in a realistic military setting. Recent Call of Duty titles have included various pop culture crossovers and celebrity-themed content that some players felt clashed with the series' military themes.

hero.headline: PSG wins back-to-back Champions League titles in penalty shootout over Arsenal
hero.body:
Paris Saint-Germain has won consecutive Champions League titles by defeating Arsenal on penalties in a dramatic final held in Budapest, Hungary. The victory cements PSG's status as only the second team in the competition's history to achieve this feat.

The match proved to be a tense affair that captivated the football world. Both teams had everything to play for. For PSG, the opportunity existed to demonstrate they were a dynastic force by retaining the title, something rarely accomplished in European football's premier competition. For Arsenal, a victory would have been historic, following their first Premier League triumph since 2004 and creating what many considered the greatest season in the club's history.

The final at the Puskas Arena ended without a winner during regulation and extra time, forcing a penalty shootout to determine the champion. Arsenal defender Gabriel missed the decisive spot-kick, giving PSG the title. The French club rallied during the match before ultimately holding their nerve in the decisive moment to secure their second straight European crown.

PSG's achievement places them in rare company. Only one other team has successfully defended the Champions League title since the competition adopted its current format. The Parisian club's dominance across two seasons demonstrates sustained excellence at the highest level of club football.

The victory sparked celebrations across Paris. More than 40,000 supporters gathered at PSG's Parc de Princes stadium to watch the final on giant screens. However, the celebrations also led to significant police response. Paris police deployed thousands of officers to control crowds at various hotspots throughout the city. According to reports, PSG supporters aimed fireworks at police officers, who responded with teargas. The police arrested more than 130 people during the celebrations. Footage from news coverage showed scenes of tension and brief skirmishes around the stadium in western Paris.

Meanwhile, Arsenal's European dream came to an end despite their strong performance throughout the tournament. The English club, which appeared in their first Champions League final in years, pushed PSG to the limit but could not convert when it mattered most in the penalty shootout.

For PSG manager and supporters, the back-to-back titles represent a period of dominance in European club football. The shootout victory delivered the club their second consecutive European trophy after a match that required the full 120 minutes of play before penalties determined the winner.

cards.headline: Thunder's Jalen Williams could return for NBA Finals if team advances
cards.teaser: Oklahoma City star Jalen Williams has not suffered a setback in his recovery from a left hamstring strain.
cards.body:
Thunder coach Mark Daigneault indicated that Jalen Williams has a chance to return for the NBA Finals should Oklahoma City advance through their current playoff series. Williams remains sidelined with a left hamstring strain.

The star guard's rehabilitation has progressed without complications. If the Thunder reach the championship series, Williams' availability could provide a meaningful advantage to the team's chances.

cards.headline: Frances Tiafoe advances at French Open after heated exchange with opponent
cards.teaser: The American tennis player won another five-set match but engaged in a verbal dispute with Portuguese qualifier Jaime Faria.
cards.body:
Frances Tiafoe survived a third consecutive five-set match at the French Open, defeating Jaime Faria in the third round. The victory came after a tense exchange between the two players during the match.

Tiafoe and Faria got into a verbal sparring match during their encounter. Despite the confrontation and the physical demands of another marathon match, Tiafoe advanced to the next round of the tournament.

cards.headline: Fernando Tatis Jr. ends season-long home run drought with 451-foot blast
cards.teaser: The San Diego Padres star hit his first home run of the season against the Nationals.
cards.body:
Fernando Tatis Jr. snapped an MLB-worst home run drought with a 451-foot solo shot to left field against the Nationals. The blast marked his first homer of the season after an extended power outage that had lasted longer than any other active player in baseball.

The massive home run finally ended Tatis's prolonged stretch without a round-tripper, giving the slugger a much-needed breakthrough moment at the plate.

cards.headline: NCAA says Texas Tech quarterback's playing status would set sports betting precedent
cards.teaser: The organization warned that allowing Brendan Sorsby to compete would make it the first major American sports league to permit an athlete who bet on their own games to continue playing.
cards.body:
The NCAA stated it would become the first major American sports league to allow an athlete who wagered on their own games to continue competing if a district court grants Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby an injunction. Sorsby is seeking permission to play this season despite the betting violation.

The case represents a potential shift in how sports organizations handle athletes involved in gambling violations. The court is currently considering whether to grant the injunction that would allow him to take the field.

cards.headline: Finland upsets Canada to reach ice hockey world championship final
cards.teaser: Aleksander Barkov led Finland to a 4-2 victory over Canada in Zurich.
cards.body:
Finland defeated Canada 4-2 in the ice hockey world championship semifinals in Zurich, advancing to the final against Switzerland. The victory was led by Aleksander Barkov, the Florida Panthers captain who returned to play for his national team after missing the entire NHL season due to injury.

Barkov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion, helped Finland pull off the upset and secure a spot in the championship match against the host nation.

cards.headline: Tennessee softball coach accused of comment to former player after WCWS win
cards.teaser: Texas Tech's Taylor Pannell claimed Karen Weekly made a remark about her transfer during the postgame handshake line.
cards.body:
Texas Tech third baseman Taylor Pannell said Tennessee coach Karen Weekly told her she made a mistake transferring from Tennessee during the postgame handshake line. The exchange occurred after the Volunteers defeated Texas Tech 2-1 in extra innings at the Women's College World Series.

Weekly called the accusation a lie. Pannell had previously played for Tennessee before transferring to Texas Tech prior to this season.

hero.headline: Trump to headline Great American State Fair opening after music acts cancel
hero.body:
Donald Trump will headline the opening of the Great American State Fair after multiple music artists withdrew from scheduled performances. The fair is part of celebrations marking the nation's 250th anniversary.

Several performers backed out of the concert series, prompting Trump to propose replacing the musical acts with a rally. Reuters reported that Trump will now headline the fair's opening ceremonies.

Vanilla Ice defended his decision to perform at a Washington DC concert after nearly every other scheduled act withdrew, according to The Seattle Times. The rapper is one of the few artists who did not cancel their appearance.

The Guardian reported that Trump proposed holding what it described as a wild rally as an alternative to the concerts following the artists' departures. NBC News indicated that Trump suggested canceling the music performances altogether after several artists backed out of their commitments.

The Great American State Fair is organized as part of celebrations for America's 250th anniversary of independence. The event had originally planned a series of musical performances featuring multiple artists.

The cancellations represent a significant change to the planned programming for the anniversary celebrations. The fair's organizers have not publicly explained the reasons behind the artists' decisions to withdraw from the performances.

Trump's involvement in the fair comes as he takes on a more prominent role in the anniversary events. His rally or appearance will now serve as the centerpiece of the fair's opening instead of the originally scheduled concert series.

The shift from musical performances to a political rally marks a departure from the initial vision for the state fair's entertainment lineup. The event is expected to draw significant attention given its connection to the historic 250th anniversary milestone and Trump's participation as the main attraction.

cards.headline: Italy cancels Kanye West concert over public order and safety concerns
cards.teaser: Italian officials canceled a planned Kanye West concert in Reggio Emilia, citing security fears.
cards.body:
Italian authorities have cancelled a Kanye West concert scheduled for July 18 at the Pulse of Gaia festival in Reggio Emilia. The city's prefect, Salvatore Angieri, stopped the performance citing "public order and safety issues."

The cancellation followed concerns raised by the local Jewish community regarding West's previous antisemitic remarks. The 48-year-old rapper, who changed his name to Ye in 2021, has faced increasing restrictions on touring internationally this year.

cards.headline: Love Island USA removes cast member over use of racial slur for second consecutive year
cards.teaser: Vasana Montgomery will not appear in the upcoming season after social media posts surfaced showing use of a racial slur.
cards.body:
Love Island USA dismissed cast member Vasana Montgomery after social media posts surfaced showing her using a racial slur. Montgomery will not appear in the reality dating series, which returns to Peacock on June 2.

This marks the second consecutive year that the show has removed an islander from the villa for the same reason. The show's producers discovered the posts before the season premiere.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen flips piano onstage after equipment malfunction during Denver concert
cards.teaser: The country singer reacted to a technical issue during a performance of Sand In My Boots.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen flipped over a piano during a concert in Denver after experiencing technical difficulties while performing Sand In My Boots. Video captured the incident, which occurred when the instrument malfunctioned mid-performance.

Yahoo described the incident as Wallen smashing the piano on stage after equipment failed. Billboard reported the technical glitch happened specifically during the song Sand In My Boots.

cards.headline: Niall Horan discusses memories of Liam Payne following former bandmate's death
cards.teaser: The One Direction member reflected on Payne's 2024 death in a recent interview.
cards.body:
Niall Horan spoke about the death of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at age 31 after falling three floors from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Horan said there is sadness, but memories of Payne also make him laugh and smirk. He revealed he was with Payne in Argentina just days before his death.

cards.headline: Warner Bros. Pictures chief warns studios against cutting development budgets for original material
cards.teaser: Michael De Luca cautioned that reducing investment in new voices could dry up the creative pipeline.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Returned Unchanged)

Michael De Luca, chief of Warner Bros. Pictures, warned about the dangers of Hollywood cutting development funds for original material during a session at the Produced By conference hosted by the Producers Guild of America. He said studios risk drying up their pipeline if they cut too deeply.

De Luca described the relentless pursuit of new talent and fresh voices as the North Star for refreshing the creative pipeline. He offered what organizers called a master class in studio executive leadership during his presentation.

---

Reason: The additional source material provided (BBC News about UK restaurant VAT, The Guardian about Ebola in DRC) contains no information about Warner Bros., Michael De Luca, Hollywood development budgets, or the Produced By conference. Therefore, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Tom Holland says he wants to help set up next Spider-Man actor
cards.teaser: The actor told Empire he could do what Robert Downey Jr. did for him when passing the torch.
cards.body:
Tom Holland told Empire magazine he looks forward to handing over the Spider-Man role to his successor. He expressed interest in supporting whoever takes on the mantle next, whether that's Miles Morales, Spider-Gwen, Spider-Woman, or another character.

Holland said he'd like to replicate what Robert Downey Jr. did for him when introducing him to the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He's keen to help guide the next Spider-Man star through their transition into the role.

hero.headline: US military disables ship attempting to breach Iran blockade
hero.body:
The U.S. military attacked and seized an Iranian-flagged container ship attempting to breach an American blockade near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, marking the first such interception since the blockade began last week.

According to U.S. Central Command, marines departed the USS Tripoli assault ship by helicopter and rappelled onto the vessel, named Touska. President Trump posted on social media that a U.S. Navy guided missile destroyer had warned the ship to stop in the Gulf of Oman, but the vessel refused to comply.

"Our Navy ship stopped them right in their tracks by blowing a hole in the engine room," Trump said. He confirmed that U.S. marines now had custody of the vessel and noted it was under U.S. Treasury sanctions due to prior illegal activity.

Video footage released by the U.S. defense department shows the USS Spruance firing on the Touska. Audio in the video captures a U.S. sailor warning the cargo ship's crew: "Vacate your engine room. We're prepared to subject you to disabling fire."

The ship had departed Port Klang, a major port in Malaysia, before attempting to move past the U.S. blockade near Iran's border with Pakistan, according to tracking information.

Iran's joint military command swiftly condemned the action, calling it piracy that violated the ceasefire in place since April 8. A spokesperson for Khatam al-Anbiya, Iran's military command center, warned that "the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran will soon respond and retaliate against this armed piracy and the US military."

The seizure creates uncertainty around diplomatic efforts. Trump had previously announced that U.S. negotiators would travel to Pakistan on Monday for another round of talks with Iran aimed at extending the fragile ceasefire set to expire Wednesday. However, Iran has not confirmed it will attend the negotiations.

Iranian state media reported that Tehran had rejected new peace talks, citing the ongoing blockade, threatening rhetoric, and what officials described as Washington's shifting positions and excessive demands.

The escalating standoff threatens to worsen the global energy crisis and push the two countries toward renewed conflict. The current tensions have already resulted in significant casualties, with at least 3,000 deaths in Iran, nearly 2,300 in Lebanon, 38 in Israel, and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states. Thirteen U.S. service members have also been killed.

The incident represents the latest enforcement action as the U.S. maintains its naval blockade in the region as part of its broader Gulf strategy. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical waterway, with roughly one-fifth of the world's petroleum passing through it under normal conditions.

cards.headline: Tentative US-Iran deal would extend ceasefire, reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: The U.S. and Iran reached a preliminary agreement this week that could extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though final approval remains uncertain.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

The U.S. and Iran have moved closer to extending their current ceasefire, a development that has already affected global markets. News of the potential agreement prompted oil prices to fall on Thursday as investors reacted to the possibility of renewed stability in the region.

President Trump holds the key to whether this deal will move forward. The tentative agreement would extend the ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though unresolved core issues remain between the two nations. The emerging deal is expected to be a major focus of Sunday political discussions.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down from the case, according to a court filing.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening President Trump's life has withdrawn from the case. A notice of substitution was filed Friday in the Eastern District of North Carolina.

Comey was indicted for allegedly threatening the president's life in a social media post featuring seashells that has since been deleted. The court filing listed Matthew as the prosecutor stepping down, though no reason for the substitution was provided in the available documents.

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A judge agreed to review President Trump's $1.8 billion fund, which has sparked criticism and exposed divisions within the Republican Party since its announcement.
cards.body:
A federal judge has reopened President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, which seeks $10 billion in damages related to leaked tax returns. The reopening comes after a third-party motion challenged a proposed $1.8 billion settlement, arguing it represents collusion and fraud.

Miami Judge Kathleen Williams's decision revives the case brought by Trump and his sons against the IRS following the leak of their personal and business tax returns by a former contractor. The settlement agreement has drawn scrutiny for lacking sufficient detail and transparency.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor, DHS secretary coordinate on ICE facility protests
cards.teaser: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration detention center that has seen escalating protests.
cards.body:
Protests at the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey intensified on Saturday as a hunger and labor strike by detained immigrants entered its ninth day. Demonstrators demanding improved conditions and medical care faced off against Trump-supporting counterprotesters outside the facility, with state police setting up barricades to separate the groups.

Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed New Jersey state police to maintain order at the site. The Democratic governor and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin coordinated their response to the escalating demonstrations on Saturday.

cards.headline: Trump plans rally after artists withdraw from America 250 celebration
cards.teaser: President Trump announced plans for a political rally to celebrate the nation's 250th anniversary after several performers pulled out of the Great American State Fair.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Saturday that he will hold an "America Is Back" rally next month to replace a concert series for the nation's 250th anniversary celebration. The decision followed several performers, including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels and country singer Martina McBride, withdrawing from the event over concerns it would become political.

Trump made the announcement during a social media posting spree on Saturday, when he also criticized a judge's ruling removing his name from the Kennedy Center and praised administration efforts to turn the National Mall's reflecting pool blue.

cards.headline: Security preparations underway for America 250 events in Washington
cards.teaser: Washington is preparing security measures for events commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary this summer amid concerns about political violence.
cards.body:
Security preparations are underway across Washington ahead of celebrations commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary this summer. The events come as the threat of political violence remains a concern for officials.

The first event, a UFC fight at the White House, will take place weeks after a shooting outside the complex and two months after another incident. Multiple celebrations are planned throughout the summer as part of the America 250 commemorations.
